Content

NOTOCHORD

  • The notochord is a rod-like structure made of a cartilaginous substance that develops in all chordates at early embryonic stages as a rudimentary backbone.
  • It is derived from the mesoderm (germ layer).
  • It is present on the dorsal side (back side) of the animal.
  • E.g. Phylum Chordata.

Key Features

  • Defining feature of phylum Chordata — all chordates have a notochord at some stage of life.
  • Replaced by the vertebral column in vertebrates (subphylum Vertebrata).
  • In Protochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval stage or is not well-developed; no vertebral column forms.

Why It Matters

  • The notochord is one of the four defining features of chordates (along with pharyngeal gill slits, dorsal hollow nerve cord, post-anal tail).
  • Its presence in the embryo is what makes an animal a chordate.

Key concepts

  • Notochord = rod-like dorsal structure, mesoderm-derived
  • Defining feature of Chordata
  • Replaced by vertebral column in vertebrates
  • Protochordata: notochord only in larval stage
